# Evaluating ∫ -2x⁴ sin(x) dx

## Setting Up Integration by Parts (Tabular Method)

I'll factor out the constant: **-2** ∫ x⁴ sin(x) dx

Using the tabular method, I differentiate x⁴ and integrate sin(x) repeatedly:

| Sign | Derivatives of x⁴ | Integrals of sin(x) |
|------|-------------------|---------------------|
| +    | x⁴               | -cos(x)            |
| -    | 4x³              | -sin(x)            |
| +    | 12x²             | cos(x)             |
| -    | 24x              | sin(x)             |
| +    | 24               | -cos(x)            |
|      | 0                |                    |

## Combining Terms

$$\int x^4 \sin(x)\, dx = -x^4\cos(x) + 4x^3\sin(x) + 12x^2\cos(x) - 24x\sin(x) - 24\cos(x) + C$$

## Multiplying by -2

$$\int -2x^4 \sin(x)\, dx = 2x^4\cos(x) - 8x^3\sin(x) - 24x^2\cos(x) + 48x\sin(x) + 48\cos(x) + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
- d/dx[2x⁴cos(x)] = 8x³cos(x) - 2x⁴sin(x)
- d/dx[-8x³sin(x)] = -24x²sin(x) - 8x³cos(x)
- d/dx[-24x²cos(x)] = -48xcos(x) + 24x²sin(x)
- d/dx[48xsin(x)] = 48sin(x) + 48xcos(x)
- d/dx[48cos(x)] = -48sin(x)

All terms cancel except **-2x⁴sin(x)** ✓

<answer>2*x**4*cos(x) - 8*x**3*sin(x) - 24*x**2*cos(x) + 48*x*sin(x) + 48*cos(x) + C</answer>
